From Elul (about September) 753 to Adar (about March) 752 BC
Year of the world 3232, after an eleven-year gap following Jeroboam's death (Annals, pp. 55–57)

Ussher finds that comparing the two kingdoms requires “an Interregnum, or vacancie of a king, in the land of Israel” of eleven years and a half, so that Zechariah's six months fall in Uzziah's thirty-eighth year.[2]
R. C. Young's tables (Thiele as revised)
Young counts Jeroboam's forty-one years from a co-regency beginning in 793 BC, so his death in 753 BC leads straight to Zechariah.[1]
Scripture gives no age, mother or burial for Zechariah.
Kings does not say where he was killed beyond “before the people”.
From the textThe KJV spells him “Zachariah”. He was the last king of Jehu's line, not the last king of Israel (Hoshea was).
